content: Drug Interactions 1. HMG-CoA Reductase Inhibitors (Statins): In healthy individuals, the simultaneous administration of daptomycin (CUBICIN) and simvastatin did not alter the plasma trough levels of simvastatin, nor were there any reports of skeletal myopathy. However, HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors (statins) are known to potentially cause myopathy, which is characterized by muscle pain or weakness accompanied by elevated creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels. In a Phase 3 clinical trial involving patients with Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia or endocarditis, some individuals who had previously received or were concurrently receiving statins developed elevated CPK levels. Since clinical experience with the combined use of daptomycin and statins is limited, it is advisable to consider temporarily discontinuing statins in patients being treated with daptomycin to reduce the risk of myopathy. 2. Drug-Laboratory Test Interactions: Daptomycin at clinically relevant plasma concentrations has been shown to cause a concentration-dependent false prolongation of prothrombin time (PT) and an elevation of the International Normalized Ratio (INR) when certain recombinant thromboplastin reagents are used in laboratory assays. To minimize the risk of falsely elevated PT/INR results, it is recommended to collect blood samples for PT/INR testing near the time of daptomycin’s trough plasma concentration. However, even at trough levels, daptomycin may still interfere with these assays. If an abnormally high PT/INR result is observed in a patient receiving daptomycin, clinicians should: Repeat the PT/INR test, ensuring the sample is drawn just before the next daptomycin dose (i.e., at trough concentration). If the PT/INR remains unexpectedly elevated, consider using an alternative testing method. Investigate other potential causes of elevated PT/INR values. Carcinogenesis, Mutagenesis, and Impairment of Fertility 1. Carcinogenicity: Long-term studies to assess the carcinogenic potential of daptomycin have not been conducted. 2. Mutagenicity and Genotoxicity: Daptomycin has shown no evidence of mutagenic or clastogenic effects in a series of genotoxicity tests, including: Ames assay. Mammalian cell gene mutation assay. Chromosomal aberration test in Chinese hamster ovary cells. In vivo micronucleus assay. In vitro DNA repair assay. In vivo sister chromatid exchange assay in Chinese hamsters. 3. Fertility: Use in Specific Populations 1. Pregnancy (Category B): There are no adequate, well-controlled studies of daptomycin in pregnant women. Animal studies in rats and rabbits, using doses up to 75 mg/kg (equivalent to 2–4 times the human dose of 6 mg/kg based on body surface area), did not demonstrate any harm to the fetus. However, since animal studies do not always predict human outcomes, daptomycin should only be used during pregnancy if the potential benefits outweigh the potential risks. 2. Nursing Mothers: Daptomycin is excreted in human breast milk, but its oral bioavailability is low. In a single case study, a nursing mother received daptomycin at a dose of 6.7 mg/kg/day for 28 days. The highest concentration of daptomycin detected in her breast milk was 0.045 mcg/mL. Based on this concentration, the maximum estimated daily dose of daptomycin to the infant (assuming an average milk intake of 150 mL/kg/day) would be approximately 0.1% of the maternal dose. Caution is advised when administering daptomycin to breastfeeding women. 3. Pediatric Use: The safety and efficacy of daptomycin in patients under 18 years of age have not been established. 4. Geriatric Use: In Phase 3 clinical trials for complicated skin and skin structure infections (cSSSI), 27% of patients treated with daptomycin were aged 65 years or older, and 12% were aged 75 years or older. In the Phase 3 trial for S. aureus bacteremia/endocarditis, 25% of patients were aged 65 years or older, and 16% were aged 75 years or older. Clinical success rates were lower in patients aged 65 years or older compared to those under 65 years. Adverse events were more frequently observed in patients aged 65 years or older. 5. Patients with Renal Impairment: Daptomycin is primarily eliminated by the kidneys. For patients with a creatinine clearance (CLCR) of <30 mL/min, including those undergoing hemodialysis or continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis (CAPD), a modification of the dosing interval is recommended. In patients with renal impairment, both renal function and creatine phosphokinase (CPK) levels should be monitored more frequently than the standard once-weekly schedule.
